what_its_for: Micafungin is an antifungal medicine used to treat and prevent serious fungal infections caused by Candida (a type of yeast). It is used for infections in the bloodstream, stomach, esophagus (the tube that connects your mouth to your stomach), and other parts of the body. It is most often used in people who are very sick or have weakened immune systems.
how_to_take: Micafungin is given as an IV (intravenous) infusion, meaning it is slowly injected into a vein through a needle or catheter. A nurse or healthcare provider in a clinic or hospital will give you this medicine. Each dose is usually given over about 1 hour. Do not try to give this medicine to yourself at home unless your doctor and nurse have trained you and set up a home infusion program for you.
dosing: Your doctor will decide your exact dose based on your weight, the type of infection you have, and how severe it is. Common adult doses range from 50 mg to 150 mg once a day. For children, the dose is based on body weight in kilograms. Always follow the dose your doctor prescribed. Never change your dose on your own.
missed_dose: Because this medicine is given in a clinic or hospital setting, a healthcare provider will track your doses carefully. If you miss an appointment or a scheduled infusion, call your doctor or clinic right away to reschedule as soon as possible. Do not try to double up on doses to make up for a missed one.
storage: Micafungin is stored and prepared by your pharmacist or nurse before it is given to you. If you are receiving this medicine at home through a home infusion service, store the prepared infusion bag in the refrigerator (36°F to 46°F or 2°C to 8°C). Keep it away from light, and do not freeze it. Once the bag is taken out of the refrigerator, it should be used within 24 hours. Keep all medicines out of the reach of children.
what_to_avoid: Tell your doctor about ALL medicines, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting micafungin. Avoid taking Sirolimus (Rapamune), Nifedipine, or Itraconazole without talking to your doctor first, as micafungin may increase the levels of these medicines in your body and cause unwanted side effects. Do not drink alcohol excessively while being treated, as it can stress your liver. Do not stop your treatment early even if you feel better, as the infection may come back.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room right away if you experience any of the following: sudden rash, hives, itching, swelling of the face, lips, or throat, or difficulty breathing (these could be signs of a serious allergic reaction); yellowing of your skin or eyes, dark urine, or severe stomach pain (signs of liver problems); blood in your urine, swelling in your legs, or little to no urination (signs of kidney problems); unusual bruising or bleeding; severe headache, dizziness, or confusion; fever or chills that get worse. These side effects are rare but can be serious.
when_it_works: Micafungin starts working against the fungal infection right away, but you may not feel better immediately. Most people begin to notice improvement within a few days of treatment. It is very important to complete the full course of treatment as prescribed by your doctor, even if you feel better, to make sure the infection is fully cleared.
special_populations: Pregnancy and Breastfeeding: Tell your doctor if you are pregnant, planning to become pregnant, or breastfeeding. This medicine may harm an unborn baby, and it is not known if it passes into breast milk. Your doctor will weigh the risks and benefits before prescribing it. Children: Micafungin can be used in babies (including premature newborns) and children, but the dose will be carefully calculated based on the child's weight. Older Adults: Older adults generally do not need a different dose, but your doctor will monitor you closely for side effects. Liver or Kidney Disease: Let your doctor know if you have liver or kidney problems, as this may affect how your body processes the medicine.
